Organic Install moved the most on its own (+2,314, +33.9%) and is now 33.3% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

ios.head: Where installs come from is shifting toward Organic Install (+33.9% vs +14.1% for installs overall).
ios.body: Organic Install (YMK · US) was 9,143, +33.9% against last week, while total installs moved +14.1% — a difference of +19.8 percentage points. Organic Install is now 33.3% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

ios.head: Expect App Total Revenue to recover in about 7 days — more of the people installing are subscribing.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is +36.0% while App Total Install is only +14.1% — a bigger share of people who installed are subscribing than usual (+21.9pp more growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to go up in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is -2.5% right now, so this points to a recovery rather than more weakness.

ios.head: App Total New Subs is moving faster than the other steps (+36.0% vs about +14.1%).
ios.body: App Total New Subs is +36.0% while the other steps are all moving about +14.1% — a gap of +21.9pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install -10.9% — Paid Install is behind most of it (-11,271, -12.2%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 184,592, against 207,192 for last week — a change of -22,600. Where that came from: Paid Install -11,271 (-12.2%), Organic Install -9,638 (-9.8%), SEO Install -1,441 (-10.9%). Paid Install moved the most on its own (-11,271, -12.2%) and is now 43.9% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -6.5% does not match new subs -0.5% from 7 days earlier — this drop is not coming from new customers.
insights.body: App Total Revenue this week vs last week is -6.5%, but App Total New Subs last week vs the week before was -0.5% — they did not move together. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (this week vs last week): Subscription -6.7%, Pay as you go -3.5%. Since new subs barely moved while Subscription revenue (-6.7%) did not follow them, this drop is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

insights.title: Revenue by purchase type — App Total Revenue -6.5% — down mainly in Subscription (-36,606, -6.7%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue was 539,410, against 577,102 for last week (-37,691). By purchase type: Subscription -36,606 (-6.7%), Pay as you go -1,085 (-3.5%). Pay as you go is 5.6% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

insights.title: Purchase type by app — Subscription revenue is falling most in YMK (-8.0%).
insights.body: By app: the biggest Subscription fall is YMK -20,444 (-8.0%, about 44% of revenue); YCV relies most on Pay as you go (14% of its revenue vs 5.6% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in US (-4.5%), while JP grows (+3.5%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is US -9,932 (-4.5%, about 42% of revenue); the biggest Subscription gain is JP +834 (+3.5%); Pay as you go moved most in US +1,160 (+10.6%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (23% of its revenue vs 5.6% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Which app — App Total New User -11.9% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total New User moved -11.9% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -11.9%, YMK +9.7%, YCP -50.3%, YCV -0.7%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total Revenue (-2.5% vs -7.6%).
insights.body: For YMK, App Total Revenue in US is -2.5% while all countries together are -7.6% — a gap of +5.2pp. US is about 19% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Next period outlook — Expect App Total Revenue to recover in about 7 days — more of the people installing are subscribing, mostly YMK.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is +10.9% while App Total Install is only -10.9% — a bigger share of people who installed are subscribing than usual (+21.8pp more growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to go up in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is -6.5% right now, so this points to a recovery rather than more weakness. Most of the increase comes from YMK (+33.8%); YCP is -12.2%.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YCP is turning installs into New Subs better than usual (-12.2% vs Install -46.3%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YCP New Subs -12.2% vs Install -46.3% (better than its installs); All App New Subs +10.9% vs Install -10.9% (better than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.
